prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You, Mia, have been asked to play a hug role in your best friend Hannah's wedding. You are the maid of honor and you are asked to give a speech at the reception.

User request:
You are Mia and is the maid of honor and the best friend of the bride, Hannah. Hannah is marrying Andrew. Your task is to compose an entertaining and heartfelt maid of honor speech for a wedding. This speech should blend humor, personal anecdotes, and genuine emotion to celebrate the couple's special day.
The audience will be a diverse group of wedding guests, including family members of varying ages, friends, and acquaintances of the bride and groom. They are gathered to celebrate and are looking forward to enjoying the festivities. Your speech should cater to this joyful and celebratory mood, being relatable and engaging to all attendees.
Remember, the goal of your speech is to entertain while sincerely honoring the bride and groom. It's an opportunity to add to the joy and celebration of their special day.
answer:
Good evening, everyone. For those I haven’t met, I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor. I promise to keep this brief—mostly because Hannah knows too many stories about me to risk giving her the microphone next.

Hannah has always been the kind of person who makes you feel completely at home: she listens with her whole heart, shows up when it matters, and somehow turns an ordinary day into a story you’ll be laughing about for years. Being her friend has meant countless conversations, plenty of adventures, and learning that “I’ll be ready in five minutes” is more of a hopeful suggestion than a reliable estimate.

Then Andrew came along. It didn’t take long to see how happy Hannah was with him—not just because she smiled more, but because she could be entirely herself beside him. Andrew, you make her laugh, you support her, and you meet her kindness with a kindness of your own. And you’ve also shown admirable courage by joining a friendship with this much history and this many stories.

Hannah and Andrew, the best thing about the two of you together is the way you make each other feel: seen, encouraged, and loved. Marriage won’t be about having every answer or never disagreeing. It’ll be about choosing each other in the small moments, being generous with laughter, and remembering that sometimes the most important words are “I’m sorry,” “I’ve got you,” and “What would you like for dinner?”

So please raise your glasses. To Hannah and Andrew: may your home be full of laughter, your partnership full of patience, and your life together full of the kind of love that makes every day feel a little more like home. Cheers!
